bundle.name: Finger Lakes and upstate New York: eight days worth stealing
bundle.description: Day-shaped playbooks weighted to the Finger Lakes — Seneca, Cayuga, Keuka and Skaneateles — plus a winter High Peaks day and a car-free Hudson Valley one. Built around the things that actually gate the region: Watkins Glen's gorge trail closes for half the year, the Ithaca market is a weekend-only market, three tastings is the honest maximum, and peak foliage is a two-week window everything else prices against.
sources: PROVENANCE: written without live web access (the session's search budget was spent and outbound fetches were blocked), so venue names, prices and opening rules come from model knowledge rather than pages read at authoring time. The URLs below are canonical references for those facts, NOT sources that were fetched and checked. Treat every price and time here as needing a verification pass before it is quoted as fact — see KI-2026-09-06-d.

playbooks.name: Watkins Glen: the gorge uphill at opening, then three tastings on the east side
playbooks.summary: Nineteen waterfalls and 832 steps before lunch, the shuttle back down instead of the stairs, and an afternoon on Route 414 with somebody else driving. The one day of the trip that costs real money, and the only way to do both halves of Seneca in daylight.

sourceTrip.name: Seneca, the long weekend that became five days

stops.title: Gorge Trail uphill from the Main Entrance

location.name: Watkins Glen State Park, Main Entrance, 1009 N Franklin St

stops.notes: Everyone tells you to shuttle to the Upper Entrance and walk down. Ignore them: walking up from Main puts all nineteen falls in front of you instead of behind, and the Spiral Tunnel and the suspension bridge both read better from below. Two miles, 832 stone steps, about 400 feet of climb — an hour if you march, two if you stop, and you will stop. The $10 is per vehicle, not per person, and includes the pool. Hold, not planned: the gorge trail is a seasonal trail, roughly mid-May to mid-October depending on the weather, and it closes on short notice for ice and rockfall. The stone is permanently wet under the falls — no smooth soles. The main lot fills by 10:00 on an October Saturday.

stops.title: Park shuttle back down, Upper Entrance to Main

location.name: Watkins Glen State Park Upper Entrance, 3310 Route 409

stops.notes: $6 per person one way, $1 for under-10s, loops all three entrances every 20–30 minutes. Daily in high summer, weekends only from the week after Labor Day to close, which is exactly when you want it. If it is not running, the Indian Trail rim path gets you back down in about 35 minutes with none of the views — fine, just not a second helping.

stops.title: Lunch at Nickel's Pit BBQ before the driver arrives

location.name: Nickel's Pit BBQ, 108 N Franklin St

stops.notes: Eat something solid now. Three tastings on an empty stomach is how people end their afternoon at winery two, and there is nothing on the 414 stretch between Hector and Lodi that will save you.

stops.title: Designated driver picks up at the Harbor Hotel — five hours

location.name: Watkins Glen Harbor Hotel, 16 N Franklin St

stops.notes: Main Street Drivers and Finger Lakes Designated Drivers both start around $50/hour and drive your car, which is cheaper and far less annoying than a bus tour with strangers and a fixed winery list. Five hours is the right block: three tastings at 414 spacing, plus the run back. Book it a week out for a Saturday in October; harvest weekend, book it in August. This is the single biggest line on the day and it is worth every dollar — the alternative is one person tasting nothing.

stops.title: Forge Cellars — a flight in the Salon

location.name: Forge Cellars, 3775 Mathews Rd

stops.notes: East side, Route 414: this is the side with the dry Rieslings and the serious Pinot Noir, and it faces the afternoon sun across the water. The Salon flight is five wines for $23 with no reservation, which is why it fits an afternoon. The $40 guided version — six wines, the cellar, an hour and a half on glacial geology — only runs Thursday, Friday and Saturday at 11:00, so if you want that one, this day starts with wine and ends with the gorge instead.

stops.title: Boundary Breaks — Riesling and nothing else

location.name: Boundary Breaks Vineyard, 1568 Porter Covert Rd

stops.notes: A house that makes Riesling in a dozen dryness levels and almost nothing else, which makes it the one tasting where you actually learn something instead of drifting through six varieties. Ask them to pour the dry #239 against a late-harvest so you can feel the range. Reserve if you are six or more — the deck is small and groups get turned away on foliage weekends. Tasting fees around Seneca are typically waived on a bottle purchase of roughly $30 or more; ask before you pay.

stops.title: Wagner Vineyards, and the brewery on the same site

location.name: Wagner Vineyards Estate Winery, 9322 Route 414

stops.notes: Marked idea on purpose: three tastings is the honest maximum and this is the one to drop. If the gorge ran long, or Forge held you, skip it without regret. It stays on the list because Wagner has Wagner Valley Brewing on the same property, so the person who has been pacing themselves gets a beer instead of a fourth Riesling, and the octagonal cellar is a genuinely good building.

stops.title: Dinner at Graft Wine + Cider Bar

location.name: Graft Wine + Cider Bar, 204 N Franklin St

stops.notes: The by-the-glass list is the region read sideways — small producers who do not have a tasting room you could have visited today. Reserve on a race weekend or a foliage Saturday; Watkins Glen has about six places to eat and all of them know it.

playbooks.name: Ithaca: two gorges before noon, then the market at Steamboat Landing
playbooks.summary: Taughannock at opening, the farmers market on the water, Buttermilk in the afternoon and Moosewood for dinner. Ithaca's whole case for itself in one day, for about eighty dollars.

stops.title: Taughannock Falls gorge trail from the lower lot

location.name: Taughannock Falls State Park, Route 89 lower lot

stops.notes: The gorge trail is three quarters of a mile, flat, and ends at a 215-foot plunge with 400-foot walls around it — taller than Niagara and nobody is there at 08:30. That flatness is the point: it is the one waterfall in the region a stroller or a bad knee can reach. If you want a walk rather than a look, the North and South Rim trails loop about three miles and cross above the falls. The $10 is per vehicle and only collected in season; the overlook lot further up Route 89 is free and gives you the postcard in thirty seconds if that is all you came for.

stops.title: Route 89 south along the lake into Ithaca

location.name: Route 89 / Taughannock Boulevard

stops.notes: Twenty-five minutes with the water on your left the whole way. Route 96 is faster and shows you nothing.

stops.title: Ithaca Farmers Market at Steamboat Landing

location.name: Ithaca Farmers Market, Steamboat Landing, 545 Third St

stops.notes: Weekends only, and people get this wrong constantly: Saturdays 09:00–15:00 April through December, Sundays 10:00–15:00 May through November, nothing midweek at this site. Build the day around it or miss it entirely. Eat here rather than downtown — the pavilion is a food court of a dozen cuisines over the water. And seven cider producers rotate under the pavilion every weekend May to December, including Redbyrd Orchard, which has no tasting room of its own anywhere, so this is the only place to drink it. Lot fills by 10:30; the free TCAT route from downtown is easier.

stops.title: Buttermilk Falls — gorge up, rim down

location.name: Buttermilk Falls State Park, 112 E Buttermilk Falls Rd

stops.notes: Ten cascades in about three quarters of a mile of climbing, then the rim trail back down as a loop. Hold rather than planned because the swimming hole at the base is closed whenever the water-quality test comes back wrong, which is several weeks a summer, and the gorge trail itself shuts in winter. Second $10 vehicle fee of the day — an Empire Pass is $80 and pays for itself in eight park days, which this region hands you in one long weekend.

stops.title: Cascadilla Gorge Trail up to campus

location.name: Cascadilla Gorge Trail, Treman Triangle Park, Linn St

stops.notes: Free, and the best half hour in the city: it climbs 400 feet through six waterfalls from downtown to the back of Cornell's Schwartz Center, so you arrive on campus instead of parking on it. Closed every winter, and sections close for repair for a year at a time — check it is open before you plan the walk up rather than the drive.

stops.title: Cornell Dairy Bar for ice cream made on site

location.name: Cornell Dairy Bar, Stocking Hall, 411 Tower Rd

stops.notes: The university has a working creamery and sells the output at counter prices. It is a two-dollar detour at the top of the gorge, not a destination — take it if the walk left you on campus anyway.

stops.title: Dinner at Moosewood

location.name: Moosewood Restaurant, 215 N Cayuga St, Dewitt Mall

stops.notes: Fifty years old, fourteen cookbooks, and still a collective. The menu is rewritten daily and there is always one vegan plate and one fish, so do not arrive with a dish in mind. Dinner runs from 17:00 and the room is small — reserve on a weekend. It is not fine dining and does not want to be; the pleasure is that a place this specific is still standing on the Commons.

playbooks.name: Keuka: Dr. Frank first, then the whole bluff by car
playbooks.summary: The winery that made vinifera possible east of the Rockies, a village square with a real tavern on it, and the Y-shaped lake driven all the way round — up 54A, over the bluff, back down 54.

stops.title: Dr. Konstantin Frank, on the west bluff

location.name: Dr. Konstantin Frank Winery, 9749 Middle Rd

stops.notes: Start here and start early — this is where Frank proved in the 1960s that European vinifera would survive an upstate winter, and every dry Riesling in this file descends from that argument. The standard tasting is $25; reservations are recommended and genuinely needed after noon, though a 09:45 walk-in is usually fine. From June to October the 1886 Food and Wine Experience is $35 on the terrace and buys you the best view on the lake with your wine, which is the version to take. Ask for the Rkatsiteli — nobody else in the country grows it seriously.

stops.title: Glenn H. Curtiss Museum

location.name: Glenn H. Curtiss Museum, 8419 Route 54

stops.notes: Hammondsport built the first American aircraft sold commercially, and the museum has the motorcycles and flying boats to prove it. Forty-five minutes is honest; two hours if anyone in the car likes engines. Skip it without guilt if the weather is good — the lake is the reason you came.

stops.title: Lunch on the square at the Village Tavern

location.name: Village Tavern Restaurant & Inn, 30 Mechanic St

stops.notes: The wine list here is deeper than at most of the wineries — hundreds of Finger Lakes bottles, many by the glass, at shop prices. If you want to compare producers side by side without driving between them, this is the cheapest way to do it in the region.

stops.title: Route 54A north up the west branch

location.name: West Lake Road / Route 54A

stops.notes: 54A hugs the waterline the whole way to Branchport and is the better half of the loop by a distance. Pull off at the Bluff Point overlooks rather than trying to look sideways while driving — the shoulder is narrow and the road has no straight sections worth the name.

stops.title: Hunt Country Vineyards

location.name: Hunt Country Vineyards, 4021 Italy Hill Rd

stops.notes: Sixth-generation farm, and the least polished tasting room on this list in the best way — they will pour you the Vignoles and the ice wine and talk about frost. Tastings are cheap and often waived on a bottle. They also tap maple in March, which is worth knowing if you come back in spring.

stops.title: Keuka Lake State Park at Bluff Point

location.name: Keuka Lake State Park, 3370 Pepper Rd

stops.notes: Hold: the $10 vehicle fee and the swim beach only exist in season, roughly May to October, and the beach is guarded on a short schedule. Come for the shoreline and the view down both branches rather than the swimming — the water is cold into July and the beach is small.

stops.title: Skyline Drive back over the bluff

location.name: Skyline Drive, Bluff Point

stops.notes: The road that runs the spine of the bluff between the two branches, with water on both sides. It is a public road, it is narrow, and there is no guardrail — do it in daylight and not in rain. Come down the east side on 54 back into Hammondsport and you have driven the whole Y.

stops.title: Dinner at the Waterfront

location.name: The Waterfront Restaurant, 12 Water St

stops.notes: Deck tables face west down the lake and go first — walk in at 18:00 or accept the dining room. Order the local wine by the glass; the markup here is the lowest you will see all trip. Depot Park next door is the sunset spot afterwards and costs nothing.

playbooks.name: Skaneateles: a swim off Clift Park, then three hours on the mailboat
playbooks.summary: The cleanest lake in the state, a village you can walk end to end in ten minutes, and one of the last working US mailboats in the country delivering to camps you can only reach by water.

stops.title: Coffee on Genesee Street before the village wakes up

location.name: Skaneateles Bakery, 19 Jordan St

stops.notes: Parking in the village is free but two-hour limited on Genesee, and by 11:00 in July there is none. Park once, early, on a side street off Jordan and walk everything after that.

stops.title: Swim off the pier at Clift Park

location.name: Clift Park, 22 W Genesee St

stops.notes: Free, right in the middle of the village, and the water is startling — Skaneateles is Syracuse's unfiltered drinking supply, which is why the rules about dogs and boats near shore are enforced and why you can see the bottom at fifteen feet. There is no lifeguard at the pier; the guarded beach is next door at the Village Beach and charges non-residents. Hold, because a north wind makes this end of the lake choppy and cold even in July.

stops.title: Genesee Street end to end

location.name: Genesee Street shops

stops.notes: Four blocks, no chains, and it takes an hour only because you stop. Uncommitted on purpose — if the swim was good, stay in the water instead.

stops.title: Doug's Fish Fry

location.name: Doug's Fish Fry, 8 Jordan St

stops.notes: Order at the counter, carry your own tray, and do not be put off by the line — it moves faster than any table service in the village. Get the fish sandwich rather than the dinner: same fish, half the price, and you are getting on a boat in twenty-five minutes.

stops.title: The mailboat — three hours delivering to the camps

location.name: Mid-Lakes Navigation, 11 Jordan St

stops.notes: The Barbara S. Wiles is one of the last boats in the country still delivering actual US Mail, to camps with no road access, and the delivery is the entertainment — a teenager hangs off the rail and hands mail across a moving gap forty times. It runs July 1 to the Tuesday after Labor Day only, so this day does not exist in June. Three hours; if that is too much boat, the one-hour sightseeing cruise is $27 adult and $17 child. Sit port side outbound for the shade and the shoreline. Book ahead in August.

stops.title: West Lake Road up the hill

location.name: West Lake Road

stops.notes: Ten minutes out of the village and 400 feet up. This is the view of the lake people photograph, and it is not from the village.

stops.title: Anyela's Vineyards for the view down the lake

location.name: Anyela's Vineyards, 2433 West Lake Rd

stops.notes: The only vineyard on Skaneateles, and honestly the view is the better half of what you are buying — the wine is fine, the terrace at 18:00 in July is not. Weekends have live music and a crowd; a weekday is the whole hillside to yourself.

stops.title: Dinner at the Krebs

location.name: The Krebs, 53 W Genesee St

stops.notes: Open since 1899 and the most expensive thing in this day by a factor of three — worth it once, and the reason this day still lands under $150. Reserve; the upstairs bar takes walk-ins and does a shorter menu if you did not.

playbooks.name: Cider, beer and a goat dairy — the Finger Lakes in February, when the makers pour
playbooks.summary: The region's cideries are as good as its wineries and nobody plans around them. In deep winter the tasting rooms are empty, the person behind the bar made the cider, and the whole day costs about a hundred dollars.

stops.title: Coffee in Trumansburg before heading north

location.name: Gimme! Coffee, 54 E Main St

stops.notes: Gimme! started in this village before it was anywhere else. Twenty minutes, then Route 96 north — nothing on today's list opens before 10:00 in winter.

stops.title: Lively Run Goat Dairy

location.name: Lively Run Goat Dairy, 8978 County Road 142

stops.notes: One of the oldest working goat dairies in the country and a real farm, not a farm-themed shop. Hold, hard: in winter the tours are by appointment only and they will say no if it is kidding season or the road is bad. Call two days ahead. Buy the Cayuga Blue on the way out — it is what the restaurants in Ithaca are putting on their boards.

stops.title: Finger Lakes Cider House at Good Life Farm

location.name: Finger Lakes Cider House, 4017 Hickok Rd

stops.notes: The single best introduction to New York cider, because it pours other people's as well as its own. The catch that ruins people's Tuesdays: in January and February it is Friday to Monday only — seven days a week the rest of the year, but not now. Get a flight and lunch together; the kitchen is farm-to-table off the land outside the window and the pairing is the point. The Funkhouse is the one to try first.

stops.title: Route 96 south to Ithaca

location.name: Route 96 south

stops.notes: Thirty-five minutes. In February take 96 rather than the lake road — 89 gets lake-effect snow and drifts, and the plows do 96 first.

stops.title: South Hill Cider

location.name: South Hill Cider, 550 Sand Bank Rd

stops.notes: Steve Selin makes cider from wild and abandoned apple trees he found around the county, and if you ask he will tell you which roadside the fruit came from. Open Thursday, Friday, Saturday and Monday 12:00–21:00 and Sunday 12:00–19:00 — closed Tuesday and Wednesday, which catches out everyone who assumes a tasting room keeps normal hours.

stops.title: Black Diamond Cider

location.name: Black Diamond Cider, 2477 Trumbulls Corners Rd

stops.notes: Ian Merwin spent a career on tree fruit at Cornell before planting this orchard, so the cider is an argument about varieties. Wednesday to Sunday 13:00–17:00 and by appointment — a short window and a twenty-minute drive out of town, so this is the stop to drop if the afternoon slipped. Growler fills if you liked it.

stops.title: Ithaca Beer Company taproom

location.name: Ithaca Beer Company, 122 Ithaca Beer Dr

stops.notes: End on beer rather than a fourth cider — Flower Power has been the region's IPA since 1997 and the kitchen is considerably better than a brewery kitchen needs to be. Winter hours are shorter than the website's summer ones suggest, so check before driving out; the beer garden that makes this place in July is a field of snow in February and the taproom is where everyone is.

playbooks.name: Harvest weekend on Seneca: a barrel tasting, a schooner and the chef's table
playbooks.summary: Peak week on the west side, priced at what it actually costs — a private walk through Wiemer's vineyard during picking, the whole schooner for the afternoon, twelve seats at one table in Geneva, and a lakefront room you booked in June.

stops.title: Private vineyard walk and barrel tasting at Hermann J. Wiemer

location.name: Hermann J. Wiemer Vineyard, 3962 Route 14

stops.notes: West side, Route 14: the older estates, the deep-water bank that keeps the vines alive in January, and the Rieslings that get compared to the Mosel without embarrassment. The seated tasting is $15–25 and you can more or less walk in; this is the other thing — into the blocks with somebody who farms them, then thief samples out of barrel and tank. It has to be arranged weeks ahead, it costs about $125 a head, and during harvest they may simply refuse because everyone is on a picking line. Ask in August for an October date and take whatever morning they offer.

stops.title: Route 14 south to Watkins Glen

location.name: Route 14 south

stops.notes: Thirty-five minutes with the lake on your left. Peak colour on this shore is usually the last full week of October and moves a week either way with the weather — the north end around Geneva runs later than the hills above Dundee, so if you are early, drive north; if you are late, drive up.

stops.title: Lunch at Graft before the boat

location.name: Graft Wine + Cider Bar, 204 N Franklin St

stops.notes: Eat before sailing, not after. Two hours on open water in October is colder than the forecast says and there is no galley — the boat is a 1926 schooner, not a dinner cruise.

stops.title: The whole of Schooner True Love for the afternoon

location.name: Schooner True Love, Seneca Harbor Park pier

stops.notes: A 1926 John Alden schooner that was in High Society, chartering out of the harbour. A private two-hour sail is $999–$1,199 for up to 22 people — which is ridiculous for a couple and about $50 a head for a group, so this is the stop that decides whether you bring people. If it is just two of you, take a public sail at roughly $75 each instead and spend the difference on dinner. Harvest weekends are gone by August. Bring more layers than you think; the wind on the water is a different day from the wind on shore.

stops.title: Route 14 north to Geneva

location.name: Route 14 north

stops.notes: Fifty-five minutes up the west shore in low October light, which is the best drive in the region and the reason to sleep at the north end rather than back in Watkins Glen.

stops.title: Check in at Geneva On The Lake

location.name: Geneva On The Lake, 1001 Lochland Rd

stops.notes: A 1911 villa on ten acres with a formal garden running down toward the water. Mid-September to mid-October is the single peak of the year here — foliage and harvest land on the same weekends — and a room that is $220 in April is $400-plus now, usually with a two-night minimum. Book it in June. Walk the garden before dinner while there is still light; it is the whole reason to stay here rather than at a chain in town.

stops.title: F.L.X. Table — one table, one menu

location.name: F.L.X. Table, 22 Linden St

stops.notes: Christopher Bates is a Master Sommelier who cooks, and the room is one long table of twelve — you will eat next to strangers, and that is the format, not an accident. Set menu, $85–$125 depending on the night, with pairings tiered from about +$49 zero-proof to +$179 for the rare-wine flight. Reservations open online and weekends go two to four weeks out; October goes further. Tell them about allergies when you book, because there is no second menu to fall back on.

stops.title: The lawn at the villa, afterwards

location.name: Geneva On The Lake garden lawn, 1001 Lochland Rd

stops.notes: Costs nothing and is the best part of the day. There is almost no light pollution across the water, the garden is open to guests all night, and the bar will let you carry a glass out.

playbooks.name: Lake Placid in January: Cascade in the morning, the Olympic oval after
playbooks.summary: The easiest of the forty-six High Peaks in winter conditions before lunch, then skating the ice Eric Heiden won five golds on for about ten dollars. The Adirondacks at their cheapest and their coldest.

stops.title: Breakfast on Main Street before it is light

location.name: The Breakfast Club, etc., 2733 Main St

stops.notes: Eat properly: on a January hike you burn through food and there is nothing on Route 73. Fill a thermos here too — water bottles freeze solid above the treeline and a bladder hose freezes in twenty minutes.

stops.title: Route 73 east to the Cascade trailhead

location.name: Route 73 / Cascade Welcome Center

stops.notes: Roadside parking on 73 at the trailhead has been squeezed hard — use the Cascade Welcome Center lot and walk or shuttle in rather than inventing a shoulder spot, which gets ticketed. Separately, and often confused with this: the Adirondack Mountain Reserve trailheads at St. Huberts need a free advance reservation from May 1 to October 31 through hikeamr.org. That is a different trailhead and does not apply here.

stops.title: Cascade Mountain, up and back

location.name: Cascade Mountain trail, Route 73

stops.notes: Four point eight miles round trip and about 1,940 feet — the least demanding of the forty-six and the only one with a genuinely bare summit you can do in half a winter day. That does not make it casual in January: microspikes to the col, and the last quarter mile of open rock is wind-scoured ice where crampons and a real shell stop being optional. Hold, and mean it — if the summit forecast is above 25 mph wind, turn round at the treeline and you have still had a good morning. It gets dark at 16:40; be off the open rock by 14:30 whatever happens.

stops.title: Lunch at Big Slide Brewery on the way back in

location.name: Big Slide Brewery & Public House, 5686 Cascade Rd

stops.notes: It is on Cascade Road on the way back into town, which nothing else good is — everywhere else means parking on Main Street in boots. Table by the window, boots off, no apologies.

stops.title: Public skate on the Olympic Speedskating Oval

location.name: James C. Sheffield Olympic Speedskating Oval, 2634 Main St

stops.notes: Eric Heiden won five gold medals on this outdoor ice in 1980 and you can skate the same 400 metres for about ten dollars including rentals. Check the session board first — hockey and speed-skating clubs take it often, and public sessions are shorter than you would guess. Outdoor ice, so it is weather-dependent in a thaw.

stops.title: The toboggan chute onto Mirror Lake

location.name: Lake Placid Toboggan Chute, Parkside Dr

stops.notes: A wooden chute that fires you off a pier and out across the frozen lake, for a few dollars a run. It only opens when the ice is thick enough and generally only on weekends and holiday weeks, so treat it as a bonus rather than a plan — some Januaries it never opens at all. Dusk is the run to take; the whole village is lit behind you.

stops.title: Lake Placid Olympic Museum

location.name: Lake Placid Olympic Museum, Olympic Center, 2634 Main St

stops.notes: An hour, indoors, warm, and it explains why a village of 2,500 people has two Winter Games behind it. Take it if the chute was closed; skip it if you are still cold from the summit.

stops.title: Dinner at Generations, Mirror Lake Inn

location.name: Generations at Mirror Lake Inn, 77 Mirror Lake Dr

stops.notes: Reserve, ask for a window on the lake side, and change out of hiking clothes — this is the one room in town that notices. It is the expensive line in a day that was otherwise free, which is the right way round after a peak.

playbooks.name: Beacon and Storm King without a car: Dia in the morning light, five hundred acres after
playbooks.summary: Metro-North up the river, three hours in a daylit factory full of minimalism, then Maya Lin and Serra out in a field. The only way to see both in a day, and it works without renting anything.

stops.title: Hudson Line north to Beacon

location.name: Metro-North Hudson Line, Grand Central Terminal

stops.notes: About 85 minutes and roughly $16 off-peak against $25 peak, so leave after 09:00 if you can stomach the later start. Sit on the left going north — the track runs on the riverbank almost the whole way and the right side is a wall of rock. Beacon station is an eight-minute walk from Dia, and the free Beacon Loop bus does the same trip Monday to Saturday.

stops.title: Dia:Beacon, first thing

location.name: Dia:Beacon, 3 Beekman St

stops.notes: Timed tickets only and nothing is sold at the door — they release the following month on the 15th at 09:00 ET, and summer weekends do go. $25 adult, $12 student. Morning matters more here than at any other museum: the galleries in the old Nabisco box-printing plant are lit by daylight through sawtooth roofs, so a late-afternoon visit in winter is genuinely dim. Three hours is right; Serra's torqued ellipses and the Walter De Maria floor take an hour of that between them.

stops.title: Lunch on Main Street

location.name: Meyer's Olde Dutch, 184 Main St

stops.notes: Beacon's Main Street is a mile long and everything on it is between the station and the mountain, so lunch is also the only walk through town you will get today. Counter service and fast, which matters — you have a ride to catch.

stops.title: Rideshare across the river to Storm King

location.name: Storm King Art Center gate, 1 Museum Rd

stops.notes: There is no transit link, and this is the part people discover too late: about 25 minutes and $30–40 each way by car across the Newburgh–Beacon bridge. Order the return ride before you start walking back to the gate — coverage out there is thin and a Sunday evening pickup can take twenty minutes to appear.

stops.title: Storm King Art Center — take the bike

location.name: Storm King Art Center, 1 Museum Rd

stops.notes: Five hundred acres. On foot you will see a third of it and mostly the third nearest the car park. Rent a bike at the visitor centre or ride the tram, and go to the far south fields first while you have legs — Maya Lin's Wavefield is the corner everyone runs out of time for. Wednesday to Monday 10:00–18:00, closed Tuesdays, last entry 17:00; parking is included in admission and pre-purchased tickets are effectively required. Peak fall pricing applies on late-September and October weekends, which is also when it is at its best.

stops.title: Dinner at the Roundhouse over the falls

location.name: The Roundhouse, 2 E Main St

stops.notes: A converted mill at the bottom of Main Street with the falls running under the terrace. Reserve — it is the one room in Beacon that fills, and you are arriving on the same schedule as everyone else coming back from Storm King.

stops.title: Last comfortable train south

location.name: Beacon station, 1 Ferry Plaza

stops.notes: Trains thin out after about 22:00 and the late ones stop everywhere. Check the actual timetable at dinner rather than trusting this — a missed Beacon train is an hour on a cold platform.
